negative_findings.description: No Hungarian trade-press outlet was found that maintains a structured, machine-readable index of bank IT contracts/vendor wins. Deal detail is scattered across narrative articles with no tagging convention for 'szállító' or 'beszállító' in the banking context (only Piac & Profit exposes a generic supplier tag).
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches combining Hungarian outlet names with 'szerződés', 'szállító', 'beszállító' returned mostly public-procurement PDFs (NAV, NISZ, kozbeszerzes.hu) rather than press indexes.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection from this cell must be keyword/NER-driven over full article streams; a tag-following strategy will under-collect badly.

negative_findings.description: Hungarian-language queries naming a specific outlet frequently returned public-procurement documents and Wikipedia rather than that outlet's own articles, indicating the search index poorly covers deep archives of Bitport, HWSW, ITBusiness and vg.hu.
negative_findings.result_summary: e.g. the 'Portfolio.hu ... szállító szerződés' query surfaced kozbeszerzes.hu and nisz.hu PDFs above any Portfolio article.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: External search engines cannot be relied on to enumerate this cell; on-site search endpoints and RSS must be used directly.

negative_findings.description: Computerworld.hu (the historically dominant Hungarian enterprise-IT title) could not be confirmed as an active, currently published outlet in this pass; no live article was surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: Query naming computerworld.hu returned only SG.hu and Prim.hu results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If it is defunct, its archive may still be a valuable historical record of bank IT deals and should be sought via web archives rather than a live crawl.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian press reporting was found on 2025-era ATM/self-service hardware or managed-service supplier contracts naming vendors such as Diebold Nixdorf or NCR/Atleos; only Euronet's own commercial pages and the MNB ATM-deployment regulation surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: Coverage of the ATM mandate is regulatory and consumer-facing, not procurement-facing.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For cash-automation vendor intelligence this cell is weak; the ATM obligation-transfer contracts between banks (due July 2025 per the MNB rule) are more likely to appear in regulatory/legal sources than in trade press.

negative_findings.description: A large share of the highest-yield Hungarian bank-technology content (FinTechZone, ITBusiness ICT-market section, Prim.hu, Forbes brand-club) is sponsored or PR-derived rather than independently reported.
negative_findings.result_summary: FinTechZone is published by FinTech Group Kft., an agency whose stated business is positioning technology suppliers to the financial sector.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Vendor claims from these outlets must be recorded as claims, not facts; credibility scoring must be applied per-item, not per-outlet.

coverage_gaps.description: Portfolio.hu (Signature), vg.hu and Forbes.hu place a meaningful portion of their deepest bank-technology reporting behind paywalls; free crawling captures headline and lede only.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Budget for institutional subscriptions to Portfolio and vg.hu; until then, collect metadata + lede and mark items as partially-observed rather than dropping them.

coverage_gaps.description: Historical bank-IT deal reporting (pre-2015) on Bitport, HWSW and possibly Computerworld.hu was not systematically enumerated in this pass; only individual old articles surfaced opportunistically.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a one-off backfill against each outlet's own archive pagination plus the Internet Archive, keyed on bank names, to build the historical vendor-relationship baseline.

coverage_gaps.description: The bank-side actor map is incomplete: coverage clustered on OTP, MBH (ex-Magyar Bankholding / MKB / Budapest Bank / Takarék) and a few challengers; K&H, Erste, UniCredit, Raiffeisen, CIB, Gránit, MagNet, Cofidis and the Posta/Kincstár channel were barely represented.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run outlet-scoped queries per bank entity and per acronym/alias (MBH, MKB, Takarékbank, BB, K&H, Erste Bank Hungary, UniCredit Bank Hungary, Raiffeisen Bank Zrt., Gránit Bank, MagNet Bank) rather than generic 'bank' terms.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of Hungarian bank IT deals was thin in this pass; only international vendor announcements (e.g. Thought Machine) appear to cross over, and mostly via Hungarian outlets first.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pair each Hungarian item with an English-side check on the vendor's own newsroom and on international fintech trade press, to catch deals announced abroad but not locally.

coverage_gaps.description: Payments-specific and card/acquiring-specific Hungarian trade coverage (AFR/instant payments scheme participants, POS acquiring, card personalisation) was only touched incidentally; no dedicated payments trade outlet was identified for HU.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Targeted follow-up sweep using payments-domain Hungarian terms (azonnali fizetési rendszer, AFR, GIRO/GIROInstant, kártyaelfogadás, POS terminál, elfogadóhelyi hálózat, qvik) across the same outlets.

coverage_gaps.description: All URLs in this slice are proposed from search results and article listings; none were confirmed reachable by this agent, and several (BankTechShow event site, Bankár Magazin) were surfaced only at domain level.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Let the deterministic liveness pass resolve status; re-triage any 404 as 'moved' and any 403/timeout as 'bot-defended but live' before demoting a source.

brief: Hungarian bank-IT deal intelligence lives in three distinct press layers: a credible business-financial tier (Portfolio.hu, vg.hu, Forbes.hu, Növekedés.hu) that reports budgets, strategy and executive statements; an ICT trade tier (Bitport, HWSW, ITBusiness, SG.hu, Prim.hu) that is the only place where bank + vendor + integrator are actually named together — HWSW broke the MBH/Thought Machine core-platform choice, Bitport documented OTP's Hitachi storage build with reseller Invigor; and an agency-published fintech tier (FinTechZone, Fintech.hu, BankTechShow) with the highest deal density but the weakest independence. Portfolio's Banking Technology and ITBusiness's Finance & Technology conference pages, plus the Mindspire transformation blog, function as pointer sources that enumerate the supplier base and the status of core-banking renewal programmes. The practical constraint is that none of these outlets tag vendor relationships, external search indexes cover their archives poorly, and the richest reporting is paywalled — so collection must be on-site/RSS keyword-and-NER driven, with per-item provenance flags separating reported fact from vendor claim.
